land.text: the Cambodian side of the Thai frontier, where the resistance 'operated from the refugee camps and from hidden military outposts along the Thai border'

predecessors.note: Democratic Kampuchea fell with Phnom Penh in January 1979; its remnant 'was forced to retreat into the jungle near the border with Thailand' (Cambodian-Vietnamese War page). The CGDK itself dates from 22 June 1982; this dossier starts with the remnant so that the border zone is drawn from 1979.

successors.note: The CGDK page says only 'dissolved: 1993'; the restored Kingdom of Cambodia took the country. The Khmer Rouge continued as an insurgency (Khmer Rouge infobox: 1992-1994); the pages opened say nothing about Pailin after 1989.

capitals.name: Phnom Penh (claimed; held by the People's Republic of Kampuchea)
capitals.note: No seat is named on the CGDK page; Phnom Penh appears only as the rival PRK's. The signing of the coalition took place in Kuala Lumpur (22 June 1982). The dot marks the claim to the Cambodian government and UN seat, not a capital in use; coordinates are the gazetteer's Phnom Penh.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The page gives no extent: 'the Khmer Rouge was forced to retreat into the jungle near the border with Thailand' and the other factions 'operated from several refugee camps on the Thai-Cambodian border'. The strip is the same 62-cell Cambodian side of the Thai frontier that the people-s-republic-of-kampuchea dossier uses for its contest with the Khmer Rouge. The KPNLF's 1979 proclamation camp Sok Sann lay 'in the jungles of the Cardamom Mountains' (KPNLF page).

region.text: the Cambodian side of the Thai frontier, where the resistance 'operated from the refugee camps and from hidden military outposts along the Thai border'

ledger.note: 1979: the Khmer Rouge fall back to the Thai border. After Phnom Penh fell 'the Khmer Rouge was forced to retreat into the jungle near the border with Thailand'; Thailand sheltered them at Khao Larn camp in Trat Province. The Khmer Rouge page: the regime 'was removed from power in 1979 when Vietnam invaded Cambodia'; Thailand 'saw them as a buffer force'. The pages give no extent, so the zone is the researcher's reading.

region.text: the Cambodian side of the Thai frontier, where the resistance 'operated from the refugee camps and from hidden military outposts along the Thai border'

ledger.note: 1979: guerrilla war against the Vietnamese and the People's Republic of Kampuchea begins on the frontier; the KPNLF forms in October 1979 and 'operated from several refugee camps on the Thai-Cambodian border'.

1982: Democratic Kampuchea, the KPNLF and FUNCINPEC form the Coalition Government of Democratic Kampuchea on 22 June. 'The signing ceremony of the coalition took place in Kuala Lumpur on 22 June 1982'; the Cambodian-Vietnamese War page calls it a Thai-sponsored agreement. Sihanouk is president, Son Sann prime minister, Khieu Samphan foreign secretary; the coalition keeps the Cambodian seat at the United Nations.

region.text: Pailin, attacked on 17 September 1989 and claimed by the Khmer Rouge on 24 October 1989

ledger.note: 1989: the Khmer Rouge take Pailin. They 'attacked Pailin on 17 September 1989' and on 24 October 'claimed victory over the city'; the last Vietnamese troops had left between 21 and 26 September. The page does not say how long the town was held.
1990: the coalition is renamed the National Government of Cambodia in the run-up to the UN peace process.

region.text: the Cambodian side of the Thai frontier, where the resistance 'operated from the refugee camps and from hidden military outposts along the Thai border'

ledger.note: 1991: the Paris Peace Agreement is signed on 23 October. The page does not say that the Khmer Rouge zone vanished; the contest is closed as in the people-s-republic-of-kampuchea dossier.

region.text: the Cambodian side of the Thai frontier, where the resistance 'operated from the refugee camps and from hidden military outposts along the Thai border'

ledger.note: 1991: the frontier strip returns to the single Cambodian state under the Paris settlement (the page is silent on any handover; the Khmer Rouge infobox shows only an 'insurgency' from 1992). Bridging judgment so that the strip is not drawn after the contest closes.

region.text: Pailin, attacked on 17 September 1989 and claimed by the Khmer Rouge on 24 October 1989

ledger.note: 1993: the coalition is dissolved when the monarchy is restored (CGDK page: 'dissolved 1993'; the people-s-republic-of-kampuchea dossier gives September 1993). The Khmer Rouge continued as an insurgency and a rival government (1994-1998) outside this dossier.

wars.name: Cambodian-Vietnamese War

zones.text: the Cambodian side of the Thai frontier, where the resistance 'operated from the refugee camps and from hidden military outposts along the Thai border'

wars.outcome: The resistance survived on the Thai frontier through the 1984-85 dry-season offensive and the 1989 Vietnamese withdrawal; the Paris Peace Agreement followed on 23 October 1991.
wars.note: 1984-85: Vietnamese offensive overran 'the base camps of several anti-Vietnamese resistance groups'; the KPNLF lost about 30 percent of its men and material (KPNLF page) and 'practically ceased to exist' by late 1987. The pages name no overrun places.

wars.name: Khmer Rouge attack on Pailin

zones.text: Pailin, attacked on 17 September 1989 and claimed by the Khmer Rouge on 24 October 1989

wars.outcome: Attacked 17 September 1989 by the 320th and 412th Khmer Rouge divisions against one government division; the Khmer Rouge claimed victory on 24 October 1989.

certainty.note: A guerrilla frontier zone with no recorded boundary; only Pailin is a named place.

sources.title: Coalition Government of Democratic Kampuchea
sources.note: Formation 22 June 1982 (Kuala Lumpur), leaders, UN seat, rename to the National Government of Cambodia in 1990, dissolution 1993; no territory.

sources.title: Cambodian-Vietnamese War
sources.note: The retreat to the Thai border in 1979, the 1984-85 offensive, Vietnamese withdrawal 21-26 September 1989, Pailin 17 September and 24 October 1989, the Paris Peace Agreement of 23 October 1991.

sources.title: Khmer Rouge
sources.note: 1979 fall, Thai sheltering, 1982-1992 coalition government in exile, 1994-1999 end; no territory figures after 1979.

sources.title: Khmer People's National Liberation Front
sources.note: KPNLF camps (Nong Chan, Nong Samet), Sok Sann in the Cardamom Mountains, 1984-85 losses, BLDP in 1993.

notes: Rebel state added by se-04-x (Cliopatria lacks it; flagged by se-04-a, -b and -c). One state 1979-1993: the Khmer Rouge remnant of Democratic Kampuchea, the Coalition Government of Democratic Kampuchea (22 June 1982, a rename) and the National Government of Cambodia (1990, a rename). None of the four pages gives an extent: the zone is the same Thai-frontier strip as the people-s-republic-of-kampuchea dossier's contest events, whose counterpart string is 'khmer-rouge', not this slug; a gap-filler should align the two (this dossier mirrors them under the counterpart people-s-republic-of-kampuchea). Pailin is the only named place; the pages do not say how long it stayed Khmer Rouge. Not recorded: Phnom Malai, Anlong Veng, Camp Rithisen, Ampil (not on any page opened); the Khmer Rouge insurgency and rival government 1992-1999 (Khmer Rouge page infobox: insurgency 1992-1994, 'Provisional Government of National Union and National Salvation of Cambodia' formed July 1994 per the CGDK page, insurgency 1998-1999), which needs a successor dossier from a gap-filler. No capital is named on any page; Phnom Penh is a claim. No ruler strip: Sihanouk was president 1982-1987 and Son Sann prime minister 1982-1991/92 (infobox) but no list of reigns. Disagreement: the CGDK page says the coalition was signed at Kuala Lumpur, the war page calls it a Thai-sponsored accord. Page budget: 4 pages. Gazetteer: the Cardamom Mountains are not in the gazetteer (unused).
